authoredFrom: PS3 (a METHOD is a scope) + PS4 (a CONSTRUCTOR is named `constructor` and owned by its class). Authored 2026-09-26. Both were measured at the SURFACE, not reasoned in the analyzer: indexed as a project, `bb_graph Start` on a method that IS called returned `callers: []` AND `callees: []` — a dead end in both directions — because the pre-wave lane pushed no owner for `class_method_definition`, so every call inside a method was attributed to the CLASS; and every PowerShell class constructor stored with `owner_symbol_id = NULL` because PowerShell writes a constructor with the class's own name, making the containment edge a self-edge the store's M51.A1 guard then refused. Rulings adopted: M59 #879 and web-family #814 (METHOD source), and csharp's synthesised-member contract for a name the source never writes.

expectSymbols.name: constructor
expectSymbols.comment: PS4: the source writes `Deployment(...)`, never `constructor`, so the symbol name is synthesised. Naming it after the class made it a self-edge that the store's self-ownership guard refused, which is why every PowerShell constructor was an orphan in the graph.

expectRelationships.comment: PS4: the containment edge the store resolves the owner FROM. Without it the constructor stored ownerless.
PowerShell class methods are virtual by default, so a same-named subclass member IS an override. The pre-wave lane emitted ZERO `overrides` edges in the language.
PS3: attributed to the CONSTRUCTOR, not to Deployment. Pre-wave this read `calls Deployment -> Write-Verbose`.
PS3: `Deployment::Start`'s own call, on the METHOD. Pre-wave this read `calls Deployment -> Write-Host`.
PS3: `TurboDeployment::Start`'s own call. The two Start methods are distinct scopes, so the same callee at the same name yields two rows from two owners.

PS9: `$this.Name = $name` is a WRITE of the member. PSD16 measured a `Class.Name` retarget here and REJECTED it: the corpus declares the same class in many files, so 151 such rows were ambiguous and none resolved.

PSD20 — the read is spelled `$this.name` and the property is declared `[string]$Name`; PowerShell is case-INSENSITIVE and the store's key space is not, so the row is published under the DECLARED spelling and it resolves. The marker is the evidence for the rewrite.

forbidRelationships.comment: PRE-FIX SHAPE, PS3: a call written inside `Deployment::Start` attributed to the CLASS. This is the row that made `bb_graph Start` answer `callees: []`.

PRE-FIX SHAPE, PS4: the constructor named after its class, so `contains` was a self-edge. Suppressed pre-wave, and the store then refused the owner — which is the orphan.
THE UNFOLDED NEGATIVE: the source spelling stays unresolvable, so publishing it is the defect this rule removes.
